section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1978
title: B. Other Causes
notes: The percentage of male victims to the total accidental deaths reported during 1978, for the country as a whole was much more than for female victims. The percentage of male victims in the country as a whole was 66.1 percent while for the female victims it was only 33.9 percent. The ratio of male and female victims was 65.8 percent and 34.2 percent respectively for the States, 74.9 percent and 25.1 percent respectively for the Union Territories and 66.4 percent and 33.6 percent respectively for the Metropolitan Cities.

The State of Nagaland recorded the highest percentage of male involvement (97.7%) to the total accidental deaths followed by Meghalaya (87.0%), Punjab (81.1%) and Assam (80.2%). The other States to record more than 70.0 percent of male involvement were, Sikkim (75.0%), Kerala (74.3%), Uttar Pradesh (74.1%), Jammu & Kashmir (73.2%). Himachal Pradesh (72.3%), Tripura (71.1%) and Manipur (70.8%). The U. Ts. where male involvement in the accidental deaths was more than 70.0 percent numbered 7 out of 9 and the Metropolitan Cities numbered only 2 out of 8.
